items.text: Morgan Stanley states it has experienced, and may continue to experience, pricing pressures as competitors seek to gain market share by reducing prices and fees, paying higher deposit rates, eliminating commissions or offering more favorable terms.
items.quote: We have experienced, and may continue to experience, pricing pressures as a result of these factors and as some of our competitors seek to obtain market share by reducing prices and fees, paying higher interest rates on deposits, eliminating commissions or other fees or otherwise providing more favorable terms of business.

items.text: Raymond James states that regulatory requirements have produced greater price transparency, driving price competition and lower trading margins, and that competitors seek market share by cutting fees, commissions or margins.
items.quote: In fixed income and equity markets, regulatory requirements have resulted in greater price transparency, leading to price competition and decreased trading margins... some of our competitors seek to obtain market share by reducing fees, commissions, or margins.

items.text: Schwab states increased price competition from other financial services firms to attract clients, including reduced commissions, higher deposit rates and reduced mutual fund or ETF expense ratios.
items.quote: Increased price competition from other financial services firms to attract clients, such as reduced commissions, higher deposit rates, reduced mutual fund or ETF expense ratios, or the increased use of incentives, could impact our results of operations and financial condition.

items.text: Edward Jones notes competition from major brokerage firms offering zero commissions and lower cost, computer-based robo-advice.
items.quote: including major competitor brokerage firms that offer zero commissions for purchases and sales of stocks, ETFs and other brokerage products... lower cost, computer-based "robo-advice."

items.text: Bank of America states it faces increasing pressure to provide products and services on more attractive terms, including lower fees, lower cost investment strategies and higher deposit rates.
items.quote: Increasing pressure to provide products and services on more attractive terms, including lower fees, lower cost investment strategies and higher interest rates on deposits, may impact our ability to effectively compete.

items.quote: We believe fee pressure will be uneven, manifesting as demands for transparency and unbundled pricing rather than a blanket reduction in basis points.
